title: Tanzanian Grilled Sweet Potato
community: Universal street snack — roasted at every market
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Viazi Vitamu vya Kuchoma — whole sweet potatoes roasted over charcoal until the skin is charred and the flesh inside is sweet, caramelised, and meltingly soft. The nutritious street snack that children and adults buy at every roadside market.
longDesc: Roasted sweet potato is one of Tanzania's most nutritious street snacks — the natural sweetness of the Tanzanian sweet potato caramelises beautifully over charcoal, and the high beta-carotene content makes it one of the most vitamin-rich street foods available.
steps: Place whole sweet potatoes directly on charcoal coals or grill rack.
The skin will blacken and char; the interior should feel soft when pressed.
Test with a skewer — no resistance means done.
Allow to cool slightly. Slit and eat from the skin.
chefTips: Medium coals — patience produces a more evenly cooked interior.
The skin should be completely blackened — the inside will be perfect.
commonMistakes: Too high heat — exterior burns before inside cooks.
cookingScience: Sweet potato contains beta-carotene in fat-soluble form — the natural oils in the sweet potato mobilise during roasting, making the beta-carotene more bioavailable than in raw sweet potato. The charring creates pyrazines and caramelisation products that add the characteristic roasted-sweet flavour.
sustainabilityTips: Sweet potatoes are one of the most nutritious and climate-resilient crops in Tanzania.
healthBenefits: Natural sweetness — no added sugar needed.
culturalNote: Roasted sweet potato is the snack of Tanzania's roadside — the woman at the charcoal brazier who has been in the same spot for decades, her sweet potatoes arranged in rows, each one at a different stage of roasting. It is one of Tanzania's most nourishing and most honest street foods.
